options: He is not afraid of anything as he thinks must have been a lion in his previous life/ he is the reincarnation of a lion/ his name is Leo/ therefore he has a mane (his hair looks like a mane)/ he feels the strength of a lion in his blood/ he is a roaring lion/ he believes that he has never re-embodied/ he would like to be the reincarnation of a lion or a tiger or a scorpion

When we was younger/attending scuola media he was studying just half an hour then he was playing soccer everywhere possible (field/corridor in the house/car park near the house)/ or playing with the play station
He never studied much although the Liceo required a lot of studying because he did not believe in it/ no teacher ever convinced him that studying was rewarding
He is 16 he does not have specific dreams/he does not have a dream yet just what he dreams at night (but he forgets about them)
He’s mad about soccer he plays soccer in anything that resembles a pitch, (in the corridor in his house, in the carpark under his house) or at worst on the PS.

By the end of the novel, Leo’s opinion of school, studying and teachers, has changed dramatically, mainly due to his relationship with il Sognatore, who makes him see that going to school and studying can be fulfilling and rewarding/ he also starts seeing teachers in a more positive light
Leo actually studies with Silvia for his philosophy and history test, il Sognatore asks him some difficult questions that are not in the book he gets a 9/10 for the first time in his life

He is disappointed with a 7 in his Italian exam and not an 8 that he should have gotten but he did not use the subjunctive tense correctly; even after the test he tells himself he needs to learn the subjunctive because he wants to become a writer and in order to do that you need to be able to use it.

rows.verbatim: Candidate must refer both to the passage and to the text as a whole — the answers the scheme accepts

options: Roscio had gone to see the Onorevole (both Laurana and Roscio knew him from school) a couple of weeks before his death/Prof. Laurana went without mentioning his trip to anybody

Roscio had gone to see the Onorevole to ask him if he was willing to report a very powerful person (un notabile) of his town (area)/let him think that he was of his town (area) who was involved in a serious crime
Laurana realises that Roscio had disappeared for a couple of days/lied to him when he had told him that he had gone to Palermo to visit his father
According to the Onorevole Roscio had documentary proof implicating the above mentioned notabile
Roscio had not given any hints about the notabile to the Onorevole because it was a delicate and personal matter
The Onorevole had not seen Roscio after that visit, but felt that Roscio was taking time into reporting the notabile because the documents had something to do with blackmail of some sort
Roscio had not mentioned the person’s name to the Onorevole.

Prof. Laurana finds out that Roscio had documentary information on a powerful individual who controlled things in the town and he realises that the double murder was a ruse to sidetrack the real issues

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at the passage as a whole, what
do we learn about Camilla?
Give four detailed points.

rows.verbatim: Camilla was smaller/she weighed 1,250kg as her sister had taken more room in her mom’s womb; her sister was the mad one/ — the answers the scheme accepts

options: She is 9 years old; she lives with her family she believes that is not difficult to be happy you just need a family and a house; she went to Alice’s house to play with her
She has a cosy/welcoming/small house with many people living in it; she does not have a playroom but she has to share her bedroom with her sister

When she is sick of playing with her sister her mom makes them a snack; she thinks that February’s snacks are the nicest because it’s Carnevale and her mom was making castagnole and fiocchetti for them they were adding sugar and alchermes

She believes that it would be better to be an only child so you can get your own bedroom you can get a new rucksack every year you get new clothes/you don’t have to wear the clothes from your older brothers and sisters

Camilla feels safe at home/she thinks that home is the place where you are safe home is where family stay, sleep and eat together home is where the children play/have an afternoon snack/do their homework home is the place that is always there waiting for you/home is where you go back to when you have been away home is somewhere that has to exist/cannot but exist
She has a twin sister/a sister called Sara when they were just born they weren’t very pretty they did not weigh a lot as they had to share the same space in her mom’s womb;

rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme also pays part marks for a shorter answer: “She is the polar opposite to her sister” 1 mark; “She is innocent/naïve” 1 mark; “She has a simplistic view of the world” 1 mark. The scheme prices this half of the ask separately, under the heading “Camilla was smaller/she weighed 1,250kg as her sister had taken more room in her mom’s womb; her sister was the mad one/”.

notes: The scheme prints the tariff as '20 marks'; the paper prints this ask on page 5 of the question booklet.

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at the passage, mention what Leo
must do to identify his dream (three points)
and why having a dream is important in the
context of the novel (one point).

rows.verbatim: The candidate must refer both to the passage and to the novel as a whole — the answers the scheme accepts

options: To identify his dream he must look for it by asking the right questions He must read/ look around/take an interest in things.
He must look for his dream by giving it everything he has got He must question all the things that he is attracted to/passionate about
He must find out why he is attracted to or passionate about something the only way to find out about his dream is to dedicate some time and effort he must start from what he already knows

Here, the Sognatore, is giving Leo the sort of “guidelines” which will accompany him throughout the novel and which he will often refer to (directly or indirectly) in the process of becoming a more mature individual.
These guidelines the Sognatore is giving also have an inspirational effect/call to action element to overcome Leo’s insecurities.

Having a dream is in and of itself extremely significant and the tenacious and passionate pursuit of that dream is of immeasurable importance: his teenage angst is alleviated a little as he has a sense of purpose; he is inspired to improve his life.
Il Sognatore reinforces his message at every opportunity, also warning Leo that sacrifices need to be made because of it and setbacks are to be expected.
It is in overcoming/conquering difficulties that we transform our dreams into reality; we grow stronger/use courage and achieve great things.

This concept is promoted by il Sognatore and is readily accepted by Leo, slowly but surely he becomes focused on his dream “Beatrice”; the pursuit of his dream leads Leo through the painful loss of Beatrice/ and the discovery of true love with Silvia.

rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme prices this half of the ask separately, under the heading “The candidate must refer both to the passage and to the novel as a whole”.

notes: The scheme prints the tariff as '20 marks'; the paper prints this ask on page 7 of the question booklet.

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at this passage and the novel as a
whole, what do we learn about Roscio?
Give four detailed points.

rows.verbatim: Candidate must refer both to the passage and to the text as a whole — the answers the scheme accepts

options: Until the night before the killing Roscio was on speaking terms with Rosello his wife’s cousin

Even though he and Rosello were related, their relationship was not that friendly. They weren’t showing a very close friendship or a very close family bond His relationship with Rosello did not seem to have changed recently
He was a private person and not very talkative even with Manno, his hunting partner, he kept his privacy and his distance
He was a little more talkative with Laurana, his old school friend, when they were on their own
Because of his private nature it was difficult to read his mind and obviously difficult to arrive at a conclusion that he was planning something against Rosello
Roscio maintained with everyone, even with the pharmacist who was his constant hunting companion, a detachment that might seem like coldness/indifference.
His conversation was limited to replies the more numerous the group the more he withdrew into a bemused/remote silence
Only with an old companion like Laurana, he would talk more easily. Presumably, he behaved in the same way (he would talk easily) with the pharmacist during the long days they spent hunting
His relationship with his wife’s cousin seemed changed in those last days, although it would have been difficult to detect change in Roscio’s laconic manner.
We are told that Roscio had caught his wife (whom he loved very much) and her cousin

We are also told that Roscio had mentioned to arciprete Rosello, that he was in possession of some incriminating evidence against Rosello and he was going to hand over this evidence to a friend of his, a communist politician, unless he did as he was told. This evidence would send Rosello to jail
Roscio had obtained the incriminating evidence by “stealing it” from Rosello’s office when he was there on his own

He later went to meet the aforementioned politician asking him to help him send a “very important person” (Rosello), to jail, and had promised him to give him the incriminating evidence. He had not been seen by the politician after that
We are also told that arciprete Rosello had informed his nephew of the threat by Roscio which leads to the conclusion that Rosello had decided to kill him then.

rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme prices this half of the ask separately, under the heading “Candidate must refer both to the passage and to the text as a whole”.

notes: The scheme prints the tariff as '20 marks'; the paper prints this ask on page 9 of the question booklet.

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at the article, outline how one
becomes a successful influencer in terms of
a starting point (one point), things that
need to be done (two points), and mistakes
to be avoided (one point).

rows.verbatim: Starting point / Things to be done — the answers the scheme accepts

options: You need to be passionate about something and become an expert on it by an in-depth study of the subject.
Participate in/be part of/join thematic groups/subject groups and link with other influencers in the same sector
Open a personal blog, update it daily, promote/publicise it appropriately.
Source/create the best material/content relevant to the topic
Share/publish/post videos/photos/posts/articles online* at the appropriate time
Always take part in/never miss a chance to go to events and meetings related to the subject of interest
Build an online reputation/gain credibility thanks to competence/expertise in a subject
Prepare a strategy/plan and analyse/monitor results from comments, sharing, views, clicks
Interact with/involve/encourage participation of the public/users/followers through chats/posts/online** and attract new users
Publish promotional material/ads for companies/brands for earnings/ payment

rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme also pays part marks for a shorter answer: “share online 1m get as many followers as possible 1m make/create videos/photos/material 1m create a page online” 1 mark; “Don’t try to do something without a plan 4m risk of not being credible 1m and not having followers” 1 mark. The scheme prices this half of the ask separately, under the heading “Starting point / Things to be done”.

notes: The scheme prints the tariff as '20 marks (5+5+5+5)'; the paper prints this ask on page 3 of the question booklet.

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at this passage, how does Leo view
il Sognatore (three points)? Why is this
passage important in the context of the
novel as a whole (one point)?

rows.verbatim: The candidate must refer both to the passage and to the novel as a whole. — the answers the scheme accepts

options: He is very impressed by the fact that he (a teacher) goes to see him (at the hospital, a sign of humanity, generosity, and real concern for his student).
He finds him funny he is good company Leo likes him.
He thinks he is “a normal person”, i.e., not stuck up, because he tells things like a normal person would/he treats him like an equal/adult/not a student/he tells him about life/he has a life
He realises that they are not so different. He is a normal person who has a normal life.
He is not afraid of being made fun of, as shown by the fact that he laughs when Leo calls him il Sognatore
He has respect for the Sognatore i.e., when he tells the joke he laughs not to hurt his feelings.
He trusts his/he confides him as he tells his deepest thoughts - story of Beatrice
He cries in front of him it shows he trusts him.
He encourages him to pursue his dream.
He is somebody you look up to/listen to, and he manages to do this without being nasty/ he respects him/he admires him.
The ultimate compliment is when he states at the end of the passage that he would like to be like him/he aspires to be like him
He is cool/ he is not sfigato/he finds him cool he wants to be like him.

This passage shows that Leo now sees Il Sognatore in a very positive light and goes as far as admitting that he would like to be like him. It goes without saying that il Sognatore has now become a reference point and a role model for his pupil. This is important in the context of the rest of the novel

When Leo is faced with Beatrice’s disease and subsequent death, it is to the Sognatore that he will turn for answers having established him to have all the qualities listed above. Il Sognatore is also the person who encouraged Leo to find his dream to be a writer
He encouraged him to be more confident, strong, to improve his life.
Development of bond from the beginning now he sees the opposite from the beginning of the novel where he was just a sfigato/looser.

rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme prices this half of the ask separately, under the heading “The candidate must refer both to the passage and to the novel as a whole.”. The scheme lists 2 further accepted answer(s) than this card shows, in the order it prints them.

notes: The scheme prints the tariff as '20 marks (5+5+5+5)'; the paper prints this ask on page 7 of the question booklet.

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at this passage, what do we learn
about the letter sent to Manno, the
pharmacist (three points)? What have we
learned about the same letter by the end
of the novel (one point)?

rows.verbatim: Candidate must refer both to the passage and to the text as a whole — the answers the scheme accepts

options: The letter sent to Manno is an anonymous letter/we do not know who wrote it contains a death threat
Manno believes it was sent to him to keep him away/to stop him from shooting (hunting).
Don Luigi believes that it could have been sent by other hunters because they are capable of that and more.
Don Luigi even suspects/think that Manno could have sent the letter to himself
All those present agree that the letter should be seen as a practical joke/the letter is joke
The pharmacist showed the letter to the Maresciallo.

By the end of the novel, we have learned that the letter was a smoke screen to divert the attention from the real target Roscio, who was to be eliminated because he had discovered dangerous evidence that could harm Rosello. The latter had devised the letter so at to cover up his elimination as collateral damage in the hunting expedition of Manno and Roscio, rather than the intended target. Rosello sent it to divert attention away from being exposed for corruption as Roscio had evidence that could harm/against him. (who + why)

Answer the following question in English.
Looking at this passage, what do we learn
about Kreshnik (three detailed points) and
what efforts did Andrea make to include
Kresnik in his group of friends (one point)?

rows.verbatim: Kreshnik — the answers the scheme accepts

options: He’s a foreign student and he’s been in a number of different schools
Having been to a number of new schools, he knows what to avoid and what to expect
He’s nervous about starting in the new school, and quite hesitant/cautious; when he enters the empty classroom her remains still and seems dazed
He thinks the cool girl Giulia is out of his league

He feels welcome in the new school, as soon as he arrives. The staff are helpful: the janitor takes him to his classroom when he can’t find it (the classroom), while the porter finds out for him why the classroom is empty
He’s attending a new school and it is his first day in a new school/Kreshnik was in 4B/quarta b
Some measure of confidence - not afraid to ask for directions
Possibly shy - doesn’t repeat his name to Fabio + nods at the teacher in agreement instead of speaking
He always has to teach people how to pronounce his name
He is thoughtful - adapts his name to make it easier to pronounce
He has moved to Belluno
He speaks Italian very well
He found a new group of friends easily enough, with the help of Andrea
He admires the way Giulia makes clothes her own
He thinks that Giulia is out of his league
He found the class better than he imagined

rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme prices this half of the ask separately, under the heading “Kreshnik”.

rows.verbatim: Andrea efforts — the answers the scheme accepts

options: Andrea doesn’t ask him the usual questions about his origins, therefore he doesn’t make him feel like a foreigner/immigrant: he’s just a new student
At break time, ANDREA makes K join his group of friends, with whom K starts to hang out, which means he has friends from day one
He invites Kreshnik to join him with the others outside during the break - effort to be welcoming
He waits for Kreshnik to join him and his friends, this shows an effort to include him with the others
He asks Kreshnik how to pronounce his name properly, probably in an attempt to have his name correct before introducing him to the other classmates

rows.contextNote: The scheme prices this half of the ask separately, under the heading “Andrea efforts”.

notes: The scheme prints the tariff as '15 marks (5+5+5); 5 marks'; the paper prints this ask on page 5 of the question booklet.

Answer the following question in English.
Looking at this passage, how does
Marcovaldo see the plant (three detailed
points)? Why is this passage important in
the context of the novel as a whole (one
point)?

rows.verbatim: The candidate must refer both to the passage and to the novel as a whole. — the answers the scheme accepts

options: Marcovaldo thinks that the plant is suffering because it was indoors and it lacked light, air and dew
Marcovaldo thinks that the plant shows signs of suffering because the stem stretched and the leaves fell
Marcovaldo thinks that the plant is suffering because its leaves were staked, like the face of a sick child
Marcovaldo considers the plant as a member of the family, a brother in misfortune
Marcovaldo always thinks about the plant every hour of the day and night because he wants to help the plant
Marcovaldo hopes it rains so to bring the plant outdoor
Marcovaldo thinks that the plant, feeling the water (flowing) through its leaves, expands
Marcovaldo thinks that under the rain the plant becomes greener
The plant is as one that looked so much like other plants its leaves were so leaf like that almost seemed fake 5m
This passage shows one of the strong themes of the novel. Marcovaldo is a very sensitive person and able to notice details of the suffering Nature surrounding him in the town.
This passage is important in the context of the novel because it shows the attitude of Marcovaldo to compare elements of Nature to his own existence and suffering.
This passage is important in the context of the novel because it deals with one of Marcovaldo's central themes: Nature counterfeited and compromised by artificial life.
This passage is important in the context of the novel because it shows Marcovaldo's desire to help Nature.

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at this passage and the novel as a
whole, what do we learn about Marcovaldo's
relationship with cats and animals in general?
Give four detailed points.

rows.verbatim: The candidate must refer both to the passage and to the novel as a whole — the answers the scheme accepts

options: There used to be no difference before between a city of people and a city of animals- cats. Roads and streets for people were roads and street for animals.
During work he used to follow cats, they were always welcome during his lunch breaks, the cat was a guide for new explorations.
He befriended a cat who possibly lived nearby in a rich house and like Marcovaldo had the habit of an after-lunch walk.
With his new friend Marcovaldo started to look at the city differently, through the eyes of a cat.
He met many cats during his walks; even though the city seemed empty of cats there were a lot of them “behind the scenes”.
He hates the city and feels bad for cats who have to live in a dangerous and inhospitable place that can easily kill them in many ways.
The cat kingdom had ceremonies and rules that he could not discover.
Marcovaldo loves nature and appreciates animals as part of nature.
Marcovaldo empathises with animals imprisoned in caged environments, this is how he feels living in the city.
In 'Il piccione comunale', 'dov'è più azzurro il fiume', 'Il coniglio velenoso'
In 'La cura delle vespe' Marcovaldo sees an opportunity to use the insects as means of financial improvement, ends up badly.
In 'Un viaggio con le mucche' Animals seen as a job/money maker. Marcovaldo is envious of his son, Michelino, when the boy spends the summer in the countryside amongst the cows.

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at this passage and the novel as a
whole, what do we learn about Avvocato
Rosello? Give four detailed points.

rows.verbatim: The candidate must refer both to the passage and to the novel as a whole — the answers the scheme accepts

options: Rosello and Roscio's widow Luisa are cousins, he said he was going to call her and go to her house, to get information about Roscio.
Rosello was shocked about Laurana's news, he listens while repeating “but look!” and kept saying he didn't know anything about Roscio and the incriminating documents.
He began to rack his brains over it, asking questions and trying to remember any sign that could connect Roscio's words to that incredible story.
He is convincing - he makes Laurana believe that he would have put a stop to Roscio's plan if he had known, in an effort to protect one of his family.
He speaks disparagingly about old Professor Roscio, calls him an atheist.
He was trying to make sure Roscio did not tell Laurana anything about him or the party nor the family not to show he was involved in something.
We learn that Rosello is member of a party and then through the novel we find that the party is corrupted, and he asked Laurana if Roscio had named anyone.
Rosello has been having an affair with Roscio’s wife Luisa; they collude to have her husband killed, so that they can marry and reunite the family property and fortunes.
Rosello is ruthless - he and Luisa ultimately collude to plan Laurana's death when she decides that Laurana does indeed pose a threat to her future.
Master manipulator - he pretends to be aghast about Laurana's news regarding
Rosello is clever - when he phones Luisa to ask if they can visit her, he knowingly exploits Laurana's infatuation with her to great effect.
He serves on the board of directors of an important company, as a legal consultant, a corporation president and as the Christian Democratic rep. on the provincial council.

Rosello is presented as the typical example of the corrupt politician. A man of respectable reputation and prominent position, who is heavily embroiled in the murky world of corruption; blackmail, bribes, favours, stealing and worse.

The real character of Rosello is exposed by the rector, who gives us a vivid and damning description of the lawyer, as well as an analysis of how corrupt the system is, and the fact that he is resigned to the reality of Mafia culture as a part of life.

Leo is going to take a train from Rome to Milan to meet his Italian friend Samuele.

4. Dopo aver comprato il biglietto, Anna aspetta il treno.
5. Dopo essersi seduta al suo posto sul treno, Anna ascolta la musica con le cuffie e si rilassa
6. Quando arriva a Milano va direttamente in centro.

8. Il giorno seguente torna a casa, contenta dopo aver passato dei bei momenti con Samuele.

questionText:
Francesca has a busy weekend ahead.
She writes in her diary, but the details got mixed up.
Write out Francesca’s plan for the weekend in the correct order.

rows.verbatim: The answers the scheme accepts in full

options: 1. Primo fine settimana dopo gli esami: ho finito! Voglio fare tantissime cose questo fine settimana.
2. Prima di tutto devo sistemare la mia cameretta. Dopo gli esami è un disastro.
3. In secondo luogo, devo aiutare mamma a preparare la cena, questa sera, venerdì abbiamo degli invitati/
4. Domani mattina, sabato, ho promesso a Claudia di andare con lei in centro a fare colazione e un po’ di shopping.
5. Sabato sera ho la festa della scuola! Ci incontriamo tutti insieme per festeggiare.
6. Domenica mattina presto vado a correre, mi devo tenere in forma, soprattutto per le vacanze!
7. Domenica sera devo preparare la valigia! Lunedì si parte!
8. Dovrò andare in aeroporto presto lunedì mattina. Parto per le vacanze! Me le sono proprio meritate.

rows.contextNote: The scheme prints the order line by line; each line in its place is one mark.

notes: The scheme prices the sequence "3. Francesca has a very busy weekend ahead (8x1 mark)": one mark for each line in its place.

questionText:
1. Written composition linked to reading comprehension (journalistic passage).
Answer any three of parts (a), (b), (c), (d), (e).
(25 marks)
L’articolo parla di un’iniziativa che ha come obiettivo la protezione dei mari.
(a) Secondo te, l’inquinamento in generale è un problema grave in Irlanda? Perché?
(b) I giovani irlandesi sono consapevoli dei problemi dell’ambiente in generale?
(c) Conosci iniziative per combattere i problemi del mare o altri problemi ambientali?
(d) Cosa potete fare voi giovani per proteggere il mare o l’ambiente?
(e) Spiega se ti piacerebbe avere un lavoro a contatto con la natura, e perché.

questionText:
3. Formal Writing.
Choose either (a) or (b). (50 marks)
(a)
Progettate di passare un periodo in Italia per un tirocinio* e decidete di scrivere all’Agenzia Scambi Europa. Spiegate perché scegliete di fare un’esperienza di lavoro in Italia, in quale settore lavorativo vorreste acquisire esperienza e perché vi interessa quel settore in particolare.
Parlate delle vostre passate esperienze di lavoro e dei vostri studi. Spiegate il periodo in cui vorreste fare il vostro tirocinio e in quale città. Chiedete anche informazioni sugli alloggi disponibili.

Agenzia Scambi Europa, Piazza Risorgimento nº 48 00192 Roma Oppure a info@agenziascambieuropa.it *tirocinio = taithí oibre/intéirneacht/work experience/internship

Choose either (a) or (b). (50 marks)
(b)
Di recente avete acquistato da un’agenzia italiana online alcuni biglietti per andare al concerto del vostro cantante preferito a Milano con i vostri amici. Dopo aver prenotato aereo e albergo per voi e i vostri amici, avete ricevuto dei biglietti sbagliati per un altro concerto in una data diversa.
Scrivete all’agenzia ed esprimete il vostro disappunto. Spiegate i problemi organizzativi riguardo a viaggio e soggiorno che vi causa il cambiamento di data; indicate due motivi per cui dovete assolutamente andare al concerto che avete scelto; proponete una soluzione al problema.
Scrivete a:
Direttore dell’Agenzia Compra Online Via XX Settembre nº 25 20123 Milano Oppure a info@compraonline.it

questionText:
Roberto is at an Italian Music Festival.
Write Roberto’s weekend messages to his mother in the correct order.

rows.verbatim: The answers the scheme accepts in full

options: 1. Ciao mamma, domani vado al festival della musica! Come sono felice! Parto domani mattina alle 8 e 30 con il treno.
2. Sono in stazione! Il treno dovrebbe partire alle 8 e trenta ma ha già un ritardo di 1 ora! Che disastro!
3. Siamo partiti finalmente. Arrivo a Bergamo alle 12 e 45. Avrò sicuramente fame.
4. È l’una! Sono arrivato a Bergamo, mangio un panino prima di prendere l’autobus.
5. Sono appena salito sull’autobus… è pienissimo di ragazzi che vanno al Festival!
6. L’autobus del Festival è stato veloce… sono arrivato!
7. Wow mamma, c’è tantissima gente qui al Festival! Che bello. Ora devo trovare un posto per montare la tenda.
8. Ho montato la tenda, è stato abbastanza facile. Ora iniziano i concerti! Ci sentiamo a fine serata! Ciao!

rows.contextNote: The scheme prints the order line by line; each line in its place is one mark.

notes: The scheme prices the sequence "3. Roberto is at an Italian Music Festival (8x1 mark)": one mark for each line in its place.

questionText:
1. Written composition linked to reading comprehension (journalistic passage).
Answer any three of parts (a), (b), (c), (d), (e).
(25 marks)
L’articolo parla di un mestiere che permette di influenzare le scelte di altre persone.
(a) Perché credete che sia possibile avere questo effetto sulle persone?
(b) Vi attira l’idea di poter diventare un personaggio di riferimento per altri? Perché?
(c) Quali sono le qualità che voi cercate in una/un buona/buon influencer?
(d) Spiegate se vi piacerebbe lavorare nel campo dei social media e perché.
(e) C’è un’/un influencer che voi seguite? Parlatene.

Choose either (a) or (b). (50 marks)

Siete appena ritornate/i da un corso di italiano in una nuova scuola di lingua in Italia.

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at the article, outline two
advantages of PC4U and two points about
Jacopo’s hopes for this initiative.

rows.verbatim: With an easy click students/families/young people who look for a tablet/PC can be easily put in touch with people/companies that wish to donate them
rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme prints "Two of" and the split (5+5+5+5), which do not agree for 20 marks and does not say what one answer is worth: judge your answer against the total. It also accepts, for less: Many families have received their new computer and it has really helped them 2m; Jacopo’s hopes Nonem; • He is hoping that with this initiative they can give a push-boost/to speed up the process of digitalisation because Italy is behind Nonem; • He is hoping to see this initiative expand and spread in other parts of Italy other than Milan Nonem; • He is hoping to get more volunteers on board and couriers for the deliveries Nonem; • Whoever does not have a PC/tablet to donate can help the cause by giving a donation that will be used to pay the maintenance cost/to buy new parts to fix the computers. Nonem; This initiative hopes to reduce the gap between people who have a lot and people who do not have enough/have little 3m.

rows.verbatim: Students/Families who need a tablet/PC can get it for free, after it has been reconditioned/recycled
Students/Families who cannot afford to buy a tablet/PC can get it for free, after it has been reconditioned/recycled
The four founders take full charge of the requests, collect the device from the donor and they deliver it to who needs it/the beneficiary
To help students/people/families who can’t afford to buy a computer and who could not attend online classes otherwise/who couldn’t participate in digital learning
It helps students by giving them technological support which aids their study
Families who do not have enough devices for all the family members and they all need to be connected/online
The digital natives have created a platform/website that is very close to young people (speaks their language) and it is very different from the other similar initiatives
This initiative hopes to give a push-boost/to speed up the process of digitalisation because Italy is behind
This initiative hopes to reduce the gap between people who have a lot and people who do not have enough/have little
This initiative hopes to overcome the issue that digital learning might arise as students will need more and more technological devices as schools will become more and more digitalized

questionText:
1. Written composition linked to reading comprehension (journalistic passage).
Answer any three of parts (a), (b), (c), (d), (e).
(25 marks)
L’articolo parla di come la tecnologia possa aiutare determinate situazioni e molte persone.
(a) Siete d’accordo con questo pensiero?
(b) Credete che la tecnologia abbia cambiato molto il mondo e la vita di ogni giorno?
Descrivete questi cambiamenti.
(c) Quanto è importante nella vostra vita la tecnologia?
(d) In che modo la tecnologia ha cambiato la vostra vita a scuola?
(e) Il vostro modo di socializzare è cambiato a causa della tecnologia? Parlatene.

questionText:
3. Formal Writing.
Choose either (a) or (b). (50 marks)
(a)
Avete letto il seguente annuncio e avete deciso di fare domanda.
PROSSIMA APERTURA DEL PARCO COMMERCIALE PIÙ GRANDE D’ITALIA Siamo alla ricerca di personale per le seguenti figure professionali: aiuto cucina e personale da sala, baristi, personale nelle catene di ristorazione veloce, magazzinieri, estetiste, cassieri, aiuto parrucchieri e addetti alle vendite nelle profumerie, nei negozi di abbigliamento e di accessori sportivi. Cerchiamo ragazzi di età compresa tra i 18 e i 25 anni, in possesso di diploma di maturità, disponibili a fare brevi sostituzioni e a lavorare nei giorni festivi e nei fine settimana.
Scrivete una lettera o un’email in cui indicate il ruolo per cui vi candidate, le caratteristiche che vi rendono particolarmente adatte/i a quel ruolo, l’esperienza lavorativa precedente, il periodo in cui siete disponibili a lavorare, se avete i requisiti richiesti nell’annuncio e altre notizie utili (es:
interessi personali, attività che svolgete nel tempo libero, lingue conosciute...).
Scrivete all’Ufficio Selezione del Personale, Via Montanari n° 30, 00054 Fiumicino, Roma oppure a info@davincivillage.it

School timetable
Andrea has a very busy school schedule.
Write the sequence of Andrea’s school timetable in the correct order.

options: 1. Andrea esce di casa alle 7.45 e va a scuola in bici. Alle otto in punto suona la campanella
2. Andrea inizia la sua giornata scolastica con due ore di matematica
3. Poi durante la ricreazione incontra i suoi amici e chiacchierano mentre mangia un panino.
4. Finita la ricreazione, Andrea ritorna in classe, adesso lo aspetta il test di Italiano!
5. Dopo il test di italiano Andrea ha un’ora di educazione fisica.
6. Finalmente sono finite le lezioni.
7. Dopo le lezioni Andrea rimane a scuola per delle attività extracurriculari
8. Torna a casa con la sua bici dopo 2 ore di prove di recitazione per il musical della scuola

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at this passage mention what is
distinctive about Leo’s summer (three
points)? Why is this passage important
in the context of the novel as a whole
(one point)?

rows.verbatim: The candidate must refer both to the passage and to the novel as a whole — the answers the scheme accepts

options: It was a summer that was marked by the silence and not by the shouts of happiness
He did not keep in touch with any of his friends
He spent nearly three months in the mountains, (in the hotel where they always used to go), this summer was the first time he really wanted to go there
He really needed silence, to walk alone and not to find new friends
He did not find a new girlfriend in order to boast about her to his friend Niko
He needed his parents and/ He needed to be with his parents with their comforting and reassuring presence
He needed to read (read again) Beatrice’s diary through which he could perceive a “picture of happiness”
He needed to find/ see what really matters and on a mountain it is easier to see it/ because, on a mountain stars are more clearly defined
In the context of the “clarity” which the mountains provide him with, he sees Silvia for the precious person she is
He starts to see Silvia in a different light, which will open his eyes to her love for him, which he had previously ignored
He seeks silence and solitude in order to assess what is really important in life in general and in his life in particular/ hence his distancing himself from things that don’t count
He needed the solitude and the silence of the mountain to reflect on all the important things that had happened in his life
It was a summer where Leo wanted to get away from his everyday life and be alone
Here we have Leo in a reflective mood trying to absorb the meaning of all that has happened
He understands the importance of the love and support, which come from his parents
He also understands Beatrice’s contribution to his newfound wisdom

rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme also pays part marks for a shorter answer: “Leo is mourning the death of Beatrice and coming to terms with it” 3 marks; “Leo is also slowly coming to terms with his love for Silvia” 2 marks; “Important for the relationship with his parents” 2 marks; “This passage comes immediately after Beatrice’s funeral” 2 marks. The scheme prices this half of the ask separately, under the heading “The candidate must refer both to the passage and to the novel as a whole”.

notes: The scheme prints the tariff as '20 marks'; the paper prints this ask on page 7 of the question booklet.

questionText:
Answer the following question in English.
Looking at the passage as a whole, why do
we get the impression that Susanna is
living a life that is different from the one
she wanted? Give four points.

rows.verbatim: Four points are required: — the answers the scheme accepts

options: Her personality was a result/ a mixture of her (strict) upbringing, old fashioned family values and the attraction of a different life.
She wants an unconventional life/ she longed for a different life with no pre- rearranged rules.
She wants a life that is not pre-set and wants to live as if there is no future.
She loves travelling but in reality she doesn’t travel that much.
She had a degree in medicine, but she never worked as a doctor.
She was unable/ unwilling to break the (delicate) balance/the pre-set ideas enforced by her (patriarchal) family/her role as a mother.
She never wanted to upset the balance of family life by following what she really wanted to do.
She was unable/ unwilling to break the (delicate) balance which existed between her two families, (her former and her current one).
She was a good cook but she did not like it to be mentioned outside the house/ she didn’t want to give the picture of her as a good housewife/ of an ordinary person.
The narrator (has always) maintained that she would have wanted to do something totally different with her life, maybe be a writer or an actress.
She was absorbed in/ she spent hours upon hours reading /in the shade of the (carob) tree /to her this isolation was her real holiday.

rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme also pays part marks for a shorter answer: “She was a snob” 2 marks; “She had studied /went to a convent school/boarding” 2 marks; “And yet she was smiling, she wasn’t sad” 2 marks. The scheme prices this half of the ask separately, under the heading “Four points are required:”.

notes: The scheme prints the tariff as '20 marks'; the paper prints this ask on page 5 of the question booklet.

rows.contextNote: The examination paper prints this question in Irish and in English and directs that it be answered in one of those, not in Italian. The scheme also pays part marks for a shorter answer: “Young people can go to cultural events they previously had no money for / It allows young people who may not have previously been able to, to expand their culture” 3 marks; “You get to spend (500€) (+1 example” 3 marks; “The Italian government is doing something for young people” 3 marks; “It encourages expanding one’s own knowledge/interest in their culture” 3 marks; “It’s important for their personal development” 3 marks; “The bonus is valid for one year” 1 mark. The scheme lists 8 further lesser answer(s) for this ask. The scheme prints these answers under the heading “Advantage”; the paper asks for 1 point on it.

options: You can spend (500€) on cultural events on tickets to go to the cinema/ theatre/ museums/ exhibitions/ to buy books and school books/ go to a live show (2 elements required)
Cultural purchases: tickets to go to the cinema/ theatre/ museums/ buy books and school books/ go to a live show can be made online
The state doesn’t decide how the money is spent – the choice is made by the students
It allows young people of 18 to spend public money on cultural events helping them learn and to appreciate new things

options: People have problems in accessing the website where vouchers can be downloaded to get free goods.

Not all people would be good (at buying on line) or be computer literate/computer savvy.

questionText:
3. Formal Writing.
Choose either (a) or (b).
(50 marks)
(a)
Durante l’estate volete fare un po’ di volontariato in Italia e avete trovato questo annuncio su internet.
Scrivete per dare la vostra disponibilità, indicate il periodo da voi scelto, il tipo di attività che preferite svolgere e la vostra esperienza nel settore. Inoltre, riferendovi ai requisiti richiesti dall’organizzazione indicate almeno tre motivi per cui sareste degli ottimi volontari.
Campi di Volontariato per ragazzi dai 16 ai 19 anni Se desiderate rendervi utili, potete unirvi ad altri adolescenti della vostra età e partecipare ai nostri Campi di Volontariato per un periodo che va da una a quattro settimane dal 10 luglio al 30 settembre 2017.
Requisiti indispensabili: intraprendenza e spirito organizzativo.
I percorsi per i volontari: i giovani aspiranti volontari potranno scegliere tra diversi percorsi: sport, arte e cultura, agricoltura, archeologia, costruzioni, giornalismo, insegnamento, volontariato con gli animali e volontariato ambientale.
Scrivete all’Ufficio Selezione del Personale, Via San Filippo nº 4, 80122 Napoli oppure a info@progettiperglialtri.it

Dopo aver preso lo scontrino vanno al bancone.

questionText:
Daily routine
This is an extract from Alessia’s diary, she wrote about her daily routine.
Write the sequence of events in the correct order.

rows.verbatim: The answers the scheme accepts in full

options: 1. Mi alzo alle 7:30, mi faccio la doccia e faccio colazione.
2. Alle 8:00 cominciano le lezioni a scuola.
3. Alle 10:30 c’è la ricreazione e faccio uno spuntino che mi porto da casa.
4. Finita la ricreazione, riprendono le lezoni che finiscono alle 13:30.
5. Torno a casa e pranzo con la mia famiglia.
6. Nel primo pomeriggio faccio i compiti.
7. Dopo aver fatto i compiti, ogni lunedì e mercoledì vado a scuola di musica.
8. Di sera apparecchio la tavola e ceno con la mia famiglia.

rows.contextNote: The scheme prints the order line by line; each line in its place is one mark. The scheme adds: "(IF THE LAST PIECE OF THE SEQUENCE IS IN THE EIGHT SPOT AWARD THE MARK)".

notes: The scheme prices the sequence "Question 3 Alessia’s daily routine 8 marks (8x1 mark)": one mark for each line in its place.
